text:
sarah: Heads-up — p99 numbers don't match between the replay harness and our synthetic loadgen on the 80B kv-batching stack. Replay shows ~82ms p99, synthetic shows ~64ms.

raj: ugh. same model/version+image?

sarah: Yes. Same image digest (redwood/runtime:2026-03-15@sha256:abcd1234). Both use model v3.1. Kernel selector log looks different though — one run picked cuBLAS matmul kernel variant X, the other picked variant Y.

mike: can you paste the minimal repro command for both?

sarah: sure — replay run (shortened):
```
./replay-harness --trace run.json --target-host 10.0.2.5 --threads 12 --seed 42
# container: docker run --gpus 'device=0' --rm -e CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 redwood/runtime:2026-03-15@sha256:abcd1234
```

sarah: synthetic:
```
./synthetic-loadgen --qps 200 --seq-len 1024 --batching-policy basic --concurrency 48
# same container image/digest used for launcher
```

emily: do we have driver / cuda differences on the testbeds? sometimes driver micro versions pick different kernel heuristics.

luis: i pulled nvidia-smi from both nodes:
```
# replay node
NVIDIA-SMI 535.86.10 Driver Version: 535.86.10 CUDA Version: 12.1
# synthetic node
NVIDIA-SMI 535.86.12 Driver Version: 535.86.12 CUDA Version: 12.1
```

raj: there — minor driver diff. Also check container host kernel flags (THP, CPU governor) and cublas_algo_search env. Those can change kernel picks.

mike: also check the runtime's kernel selector logs. I remember we log fallback reasons. Did the selector prefer deterministic kernels for one run?

sarah: attached snippet from runtime log (selector lines):
```
[ks] select_matmul: requested=auto, picked=cuBLAS_GEMM_TUNED_Y, reason=heuristic:workspace>8MB
[ks] select_matmul: requested=auto, picked=cuBLAS_GEMM_TUNED_X, reason=fallback:driver reported algo mismatch
```

emily: interesting — fallback path often happens when cuBLAS reports fewer workspace lanes available. That can be due to available GPU memory fragmentation or different CUDA driver scheduler behavior.

luis: another thing — KV cache warmup. Replay harness replays many similar prefixes which keeps KV cache hot; however our synthetic run uses shuffled prompts, causing more KV thrash. Cold KV fills increase per-token time especially on p99.

raj: good point. Can we make the synthetic run use the same prefix distribution as replay? or pre-warm KV by running a warmup phase that hits popular prefixes?

sarah: tried pre-warm (1000 requests of common prefixes) — p99 improved from 82ms -> 70ms but still not 64ms.

mike: still a residual ~6ms. Could be CPU-side batching thread scheduling (cpu governor / irqbalance). Are both machines using "performance" governor and isolcpus same config?

luis: host-level diffs I found:
- replay host: CPU governor=performance, THP=never, RPS pinned, container runtime runc 1.6.0
- synthetic host: CPU governor=ondemand, THP=always, container runtime runc 1.7.0

emily: THP can add variance on first-touch memory allocation. Disable it for benchmarks: echo never > /sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/enabled. Also set governor=performance.

raj: we should also lock down: driver version, cuda toolkit version, container image digest, runtime (runc/crun), kernel cmdline flags (like default_hugepages, rcu_nocbs) and docker run flags (—shm-size). Make a checklist to ensure apples-to-apples.

sarah: agreed. Proposed minimal checklist for loadtest parity:
- identical driver + CUDA (exact package+build)
- identical container image digest and runtime (runc/crun versions)
- same kernel cmdline + THP disabled + CPU governor=performance
- same docker/shm/cgroup limits and ulimits
- disable hyperthreading or pin threads consistently
- identical batching config (max_batch_tokens, latency_cap_ms) and kernel selector envs (e.g., CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG, CUBLAS_ALGO_SEARCH)
- identical KV warmup phase (seeded or fixed prefix set)

mike: add: collect NVTX traces and perf counters for both runs and diff them. NVTX shows where time goes (kernel vs memcpy vs dispatch).

sarah: i ran nvprof/NVTX for both; high level: replay had more memcpy H2D but lower kernel time variance; synthetic had occasional long kernel runs (outliers) correlating with the 'fallback' kernel picks.

raj: action items: 1) snapshot host driver+kernel+runtime on both nodes and store as golden metadata; 2) re-run synthetic after aligning host config (THP/governor/driver) + KV pre-warm; 3) capture NVTX traces for both; 4) surface kernel selector logs with --ks-verbose.

emily: i'll add a quick script to produce the golden snapshot:
```
#!/bin/bash
uname -a > host-info.txt
cat /proc/cmdline >> host-info.txt
cat /sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/enabled >> host-info.txt
nvidia-smi -q >> host-info.txt
docker info >> host-info.txt
runc --version >> host-info.txt
```

luis: +1. Also store docker inspect of the launched container and `nvidia-container-cli info`.

ci-bot: scheduled: eng-runtime/testbed-parity-recheck on 2026-05-12T15:00:00Z by emily

mike: one more nuance — kernel selector picks can be non-deterministic if we rely on heuristics that probe runtime performance. For absolute apples-to-apples, pin selector policy to deterministic mode for comparison runs: `--kernelselector-mode=deterministic`.

raj: great call. let's keep that for initial A/B. If deterministic still differs, we have a bug in selector or driver.

sarah: thanks all — i'll run the checklist on both nodes, re-run synthetic with KV warmup + deterministic selector, attach nvtx and selector logs here. If still >2ms delta we'll open a perf regression ticket.

emily: thanks, ping when you have traces. :thumbsup:
